description: Cameco owns a 49% interest in Westinghouse Electric Company in a strategic partnership with Brookfield, expanding its participation downstream into fuel fabrication and reactor technology (Cameco FY2025 Annual Information Form).

Cameco (40%) and Kazatomprom (60%) jointly own JV Inkai, a material Kazakh in-situ recovery uranium operation; Cameco lifts its proportionate share of Inkai output (Cameco FY2025 Annual Information Form).

Cameco owns a 49% interest in GLE (with an unexercised option to reach 75%) and is its commercial lead; GLE is the exclusive worldwide licensee of the SILEX laser-enrichment technology (Cameco FY2025 Annual Information Form).
Silex Systems owns the remaining 51% of GLE and is the SILEX technology licensor and technology lead for the laser-enrichment project (Cameco FY2025 Annual Information Form).

Centrus sources a significant portion of the LEU it delivers to customers under the TENEX Supply Contract (Enriched Product Transitional Supply Contract with TENEX, signed 2011-03-23, running through 2028); its FY2025 10-K states other supply sources are not sufficient to replace the TENEX supply.
Centrus holds a long-term Orano Supply Agreement (signed 2018) for supply of SWU contained in LEU, one of the non-Russian supply sources named in its FY2025 10-K.

JV KATCO LLP, the Moinkum/South Tortkuduk in-situ recovery uranium operation in Kazakhstan, is jointly owned by Orano and Kazatomprom; Kazatomprom holds a 49.00% equity interest per its FY2025 IFRS financial statements (note 22, associates), with Orano holding the controlling interest and consolidating Katco (Orano's FY2025 consolidated financial statements name "Katco mining company and its shareholders, Orano and NAC Kazatomprom JSC" and record Kazatomprom's stake as a non-controlling interest of EUR 318 million at 31 December 2025).

JV "South Mining Chemical Company" LLP (SMCC), which holds the subsoil use rights to the Akdala uranium deposit in Kazakhstan, is owned 30% by Kazatomprom and 70% by Uranium One Group JSC, a subsidiary of the Rosatom State Corporation; Kazatomprom's FY2025 Operating and Financial Review states the Akdala SUA "belong[s] to JV ‘SMCC’ LLP (Kazatomprom – 30%, Uranium One – 70%)".

CGN Mining holds 49% of two Kazakh uranium mining joint ventures alongside Kazatomprom's 51%: Semizbay-U LLP (the Semizbay and Irkol mines) and Mining Company "Ortalyk" LLP (Central Mynkuduk and Zhalpak). CGN Mining's interim results for the six months ended 30 June 2025 state "the Group was interested in 49% of the equity interest of Semizbay-U... The remaining 51% equity interest of Semizbay-U is held by Kazatomprom", and the identical 49/51 structure for Ortalyk. Recorded as ONE edge because this map keys relationships on (from, to, type) and two rows for the same pair would collapse on merge, losing one of the two joint ventures.

EDF's FY2025 consolidated financial statements (note 8, Goodwill/intangibles section) state: "Non-controlling interests in Framatome, owned 80.5% by the Group via EDF SA, correspond to the 19.5% share held by Mitsubishi Heavy Industries." EDF bought out Assystem's remaining minority stake in Framatome for EUR 205 million in 2024 (cash flow statement note 3), consistent with the 80.5% figure.

Orano's FY2025 consolidated financial statements (related-party note, "Relations with the French State and state-owned companies") state: "transactions with EDF concern the front end of the nuclear fuel cycle (uranium sales, conversion and enrichment services) and the back end of the cycle (used fuel shipping, storage, treatment and recycling services)." EDF's own FY2025 FS (note 22.1.2) independently corroborates: "The EDF group's relations with public sector entities mainly concern Orano with: the front-end of the nuclear fuel cycle (uranium supplies, conversion and enrichment services)..."

Orano's FY2025 FS state Orano and EDF have "a master treatment/recycling agreement known as the 'ATR Contract' with EDF, which specifies the terms of the industrial cooperation between them in the field of treatment/recycling until 2040. As part of this agreement, in October 2024, Orano and EDF signed an implementation contract... for the 2024-2026 period." EDF's own FY2025 FS (note 14.1.1.1) independently corroborates and quantifies this: "the nominal quantities to be processed by Orano Recyclage at the request of EDF, totalling approximately 1,100 tonnes per year... Expenses are mainly measured based on forecast physical flows... with reference to the contracts with Orano Recyclage which define the terms of application of the framework agreement for the period 2008-2040." Reprocessing occurs at Orano's La Hague site.

Urenco's FY2025 annual report (Chief Executive Officer's review) states: "In the last 12 months, we have signed a number of significant, new long-term contracts... These contracts include... a new contract with EDF for its fleet of reactors in France and in the UK - our largest ever contract." The Chair's foreword corroborates: "This included our largest ever contract, which was signed publicly with EDF." This is a sourced enrichment-supply dependency edge naming Urenco's largest disclosed customer, closing gap-10-2.

Framatome's official press release (framatome.com, 2018-05-23), "France: Framatome to supply EDF with Enriched Reprocessed Uranium fuel assemblies," states Framatome signed a contract "designing, fabricating and supplying EDF with fuel assemblies using enriched reprocessed uranium" over the period 2023 to 2032, manufactured at Framatome's Romans-sur-Isere plant using uranium derived from reprocessing of used fuel at La Hague. This is a first-party disclosure naming both parties and the specific fuel-fabrication activity, though it documents one fuel product line (ERU-based assemblies) rather than Framatome's full standard-fuel supply to EDF's fleet. NOTE ON EVIDENCE AGE AND WHY: the citation is a 2018 press release covering a 2023-2032 supply period, so it is in force now but is not a current-year document. EDF's own FY2025 consolidated financial statements never name Framatome as its fuel fabricator, because Framatome is 80.5% owned and consolidated, so intercompany fuel transactions are eliminated. The relationship is real but structurally INVISIBLE in the consolidated accounts, which is why a subsidiary press release is the available source.
